scenes.narration: Safeguard. Compliant privacy and payment gateway for Stellar confidential tokens.

Every bank, fund and fintech on the planet is being asked the same question. Can you move money onto a public blockchain without publishing your clients' balances? Confidential tokens on Stellar finally answer yes. Transactions are encrypted, amounts and balances are hidden, and the transfer still settles on a public ledger. But privacy creates a new problem, and it is the one that actually kills deals. If nobody can see the transfer, how does anyone prove it was allowed? Regulators do not accept trust us. And compliance cannot be a screenshot.

Most compliance tooling answers this with a report. A dashboard. Something a human reads after the fact. That is the wrong shape entirely. A confidential operation needs a decision at the moment it happens, inside the transaction, before a single unit moves. And if that decision cannot be made, the operation must not proceed. Not flagged. Not logged. Not proceed.

Safeguard delivers that decision layer through a modern four-tier architecture. First, safeguard-contracts: Soroban smart contracts providing a payment gateway, spend-cap escrow, and fail-closed policy hooks. Second, safeguard-backend: a TypeScript SDK and simulation API that validates transfers before submission. Third, safeguard-dashboard: a live Next.js 14 institutional console on Vercel for treasury management and audit oversight. And fourth, safeguard-docs: a developer hub running the real policy engine in the browser.

The execution flow is strictly one-way and fail-closed. A client application or automated treasury invokes the Soroban payment gateway. The contract verifies that the transfer does not exceed active spend caps, checks timelocks, and calls the compliance hooks. The hooks ask the policy engine one question: is this account authorized? One call, one boolean. If anything is amiss, expired timelocks, exceeded caps, sanctions matches, or frozen accounts, the transaction reverts immediately.

Here is the property that makes the system audit-grade: there is no unknown state. An unbound token reverts with code two. An account frozen, code four. An exceeded spend cap, code twenty. An active timelock, code twenty-one. Across Soroban contracts, the TypeScript SDK, and the Next.js console, two hundred and seventy structured error codes provide deterministic, machine-checked diagnostics. Codes are never reused, ensuring that an audit record from years ago retains its precise original meaning.

For operational teams, Safeguard provides a production-grade Web3 console, deployed live on Vercel. Connected directly to Stellar Testnet, the dashboard allows compliance officers and treasury managers to monitor active spend caps, inspect escrow timelocks, review flagged events, and test policy decisions interactively. No command line required, no opaque ledger queries.

Alongside the console, our documentation hub hosts the client-side simulator. Choose an account's jurisdiction, status, or sanctions risk, and watch the engine decide in real-time. Compliant parties are approved; sanctioned or frozen accounts are instantly blocked, with complete rule attribution. A twenty-four test suite verifies that the browser simulator reproduces our on-chain golden fixtures with zero drift.

None of this is hypothetical. The entire contract suite is deployed on Stellar Testnet and actively monitored. Our ten-point automated verification suite proves live ledger responsiveness and fail-closed guarantees without needing private keys. Over eight hundred and fifty tests run across all four repositories, and release-profile optimizations keep compliant payment execution down to approximately a thousandth of an XLM.

The entire Safeguard organization is fully open source. We restructured the project into four clean, focused repositories with continuous integration on every one. To foster community growth, we created fifty-two structured contribution issues tagged with Stellar Wave labels and complexity ratings, covering property testing, SDK extensions, and advanced telemetry.

Privacy and compliance are no longer a trade-off. Safeguard provides confidential payments by default, compliance by construction, and cryptographic auditability after the fact. The contracts are live on Stellar Testnet, the dashboard is running on Vercel, and the repositories are open today. Come build the future of compliant DeFi on Stellar.
